text:
Ava: Thanks everyone for joining the all-hands earlier. I'll keep this thread open for follow-ups on the strategy Q&A — ask anything about mission, positioning, competitors, go-to-market.
Priya: quick one — how narrowly should teams aim to optimize for latency vs cost? we have feature requests asking for 'lowest latency' mode.
Ava: short answer: tiered. prioritize latency for user-facing features; cost-first for batch/analytics. we want clear defaults per product type.
Diego: can we get a decision doc on default profiles? several PMs asked.
Samir: I'll own a doc with perf targets + quantization tradeoffs. ETA end of week.
Zoe: curious about competitive positioning — are we leaning into 'developer-first' messaging or 'enterprise reliability' for sales motion?
Mark: both. PLG to drive adoption, but sales needs differentiated SLA + private deployment pitch.
Ava: exactly. our public story is developer velocity + predictable economics. sales adds enterprise controls and SLAs.
Priya: does that mean marketing will change website copy? current hero is pretty product-y.
Diego: already in motion — new copy emphasizes 'predictable inference cost' and 'multi-environment same API'.
Zoe: for model catalog: how much curated models are we committing to vs customer BYO models?
Samir: we curate a small set of verified models for latency/cost guarantees. BYO allowed but with caveats (no SLA).
Priya: can we get a short FAQ to share with teams building integrations?
Diego: yes, will draft an FAQ and post it in #devex.
Zoe: competitors keep undercutting on price. how do we respond — discount or product differentiation?
Ava: we win on predictable unit economics and operational tooling. price plays are short-term; double down on features that save customers money (batching, caching, routing).
Mark: we'll keep a price desk for strategic deals but won't race to the bottom in self-serve.
Priya: question on Private deployments: what's the minimum commitment and timeline?
Ava: typical on-prem proof-of-concept is 3 months; production deployments negotiated. Ops will share a template.
Samir: technical note: private mode requires different telemetry — we provide auditing hooks but not telemetry by default unless configured.
Zoe: for roadmap clarity — will Optimize (cost/perf toolkit) be a paid add-on or bundled?
Diego: Optimize will have a free tier with recommendations and a paid tier with automated tuning and premium alerts.
Priya: can we have a single canonical link for 'how to pick a model for production' — several new hires confused.
Samir: I'll add a short playbook to the engineering handbook and link here when done.
Zoe: thanks. last one — any changes to the fallback policy? some apps saw a shift in latency during region failover.
Samir: working on smarter routing that prefers compatible quantized variants before cross-region failover. rollout in next sprint.
Ava: great thread — keep questions coming. i'll compile common threads and send a short follow-up email with links.
ops-bot: All-hands follow-up doc posted: https://redwood.internal/wiki/all-hands-2026-03-strategy
Priya: thanks @Ava and team :raised_hands: 
Mark: appreciate the clarity — will sync with AE team.
Zoe: looking forward to the playbook link.
Samir: posted the perf targets doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/perf-targets-2026
Diego: posted the FAQ draft in #devex, feedback welcome.
Ava: closing loop — if anyone wants to volunteer to help with the customer FAQ, DM me.
Zoe: I'll take a pass on it later today.
Priya: same here.
Mark: will add sales objections we've heard.
Ava: thanks everyone :heart:
